overview: S08 is the server's authoritative position correction and the landing pad for every movement flag: setback, phase and speed checks all terminate in a rubberband teleport. On the OUT side, anticheats do three things with it: record the exact teleported coordinates and the teleport id, bracket the teleport between transaction packets so the confirm can be time-ordered, and verify that the client's C06 confirm matches the coordinates the server actually sent. The four checks below cover that full pipeline, from the packet listener that converts relative flags to absolute positions (Grim) to the confirm verifier that kicks on a mismatch (CheaterDeleter).

checks.name: PacketServerTeleport (Grim)
checks.purpose: Tracks every outgoing player teleport so the simulation knows the client's authoritative position and can enforce it in later movement checks.
checks.how_it_works: Listens on the OUT side for the player position-and-look packet, seeds the player's tracked position on join, converts relative flags to absolute coordinates (rewriting the packet for 1.8-era clients), and brackets the teleport with a transaction sandwich so the exact arrival tick is known. Vehicle teleports are recorded against the same transaction stream.
checks.detects: Teleport-based desync where the client's reported position diverges from the server's authoritative teleport target.
checks.variations: Artemis and CheaterDeleter record the same OUT teleport event; Grim additionally re-encodes the packet so its own simulation never sees relative coordinates.

checks.name: TeleportVerifierCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Verifies that the client's teleport confirm returns the exact coordinates the server sent, kicking on any mismatch.
checks.how_it_works: Stores the target position (resolving relative flags against the player's current position) keyed by the S08 teleport id. When the client sends the matching teleport-confirm packet, the check compares each axis of the attached movement packet against the stored target: absolute axes must match exactly, relative axes must be within 10 blocks. Any disagreement kicks the player.
checks.detects: Cancel-and-spoof teleport bypasses where a client accepts the teleport id but reports a different position, and disabler-style teleport manipulation.
checks.variations: Grim instead flags and sets back; BetterAnticheat resolves teleports inside its confirmation tracker before comparing movement.

checks.name: TeleportTracker (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Compensates outgoing teleport packets so movement checks can distinguish a teleport from an illegal position jump.
checks.how_it_works: On the OUT side it wraps the position-and-look packet (plus entity teleport and rotation packets for the player) into a Teleport record that is only added to the eligible list after the confirmation tracker's pre-transaction fires. On the IN side, every flying packet is matched against eligible teleports: onGround flag, absolute coordinates and rotations must line up, with a 2.0E-4 leniency for relative axes when the player did not send a position packet the previous tick. Teleports that never match become a missedTeleport state for the checks.
checks.detects: Movement spoofing that fakes teleport confirms, and the desync that follows when a client skips or reorders teleport confirmation.
checks.variations: Grim's SetbackTeleportUtil keeps an explicit queue of sent teleports; CheaterDeleter verifies confirms immediately and kicks.

checks.name: TeleportPreProcessor (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Feeds server teleport and entity-teleport packets into the movement holder so position checks run against the post-teleport state.
checks.how_it_works: Handles the OUT position packet and the player's entity-teleport packet. For entity teleports it registers a transaction-confirmed action: on the pre side it moves the last velocity into lastVelocity, installs the teleported position as the current movement and location, and marks the movement as teleport-processed; the post side clears that flag once the client confirms.
checks.detects: Cheats that depend on the anticheat not knowing the server moved the player, and velocity residue that should be cleared by a teleport.
checks.variations: Grim uses a transaction sandwich on the OUT packet itself; Artemis applies the teleport on the confirm instead of at send time.
